properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock comprises Carboniferous sedimentary strata of the Strathclyde Group (sandstone, siltstone, and mudstone) overlain by dense glacial till. Primary structural masonry is Craigleith sandstone (a highly siliceous, quartzitic buff-grey pale sandstone with high compressive strength) combined with Hailes sandstone for structural backing. Mortar is traditional non-hydraulic slaked lime and coarse river sand. The central equestrian monument plinth is composed of polished pink Peterhead granite blocks set upon a hard sandstone sub-base.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Charlotte Square Garden interior dominated by mature broadleaf specimens: *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime), and *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm). Late September phenology: dense canopies exhibiting early autumn senescence, chlorotic pale-yellow to ochre leaf margins, patchy crown thinning, and initial leaf-litter dispersal across the manicured *Lolium perenne* and *Festuca rubra* turf lawn.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical urban square composition dominated by the central monument of West Register House (formerly St George's Church). The central edifice presents an imposing tetrastyle Ionic portico with unfluted/fluted giant order columns, an unadorned frieze, triangular pediment, and a monumental central copper dome supported on an arcaded drum with peristyle Corinthian colonnettes and an octagonal lantern cupola. Flanking wings display symmetrical, three-storey plus attic and basement Georgian townhouse facades: rusticated ashlar ground storeys with round-arched openings, piano nobile with moulded architraves and pedimented central bays, regular 6-over-6 and 12-pane timber sash-and-case fenestration, projecting continuous stone stringcourses, cornice entablatures, balustraded parapets, dormer-punctuated Mansard roofs, and tall ashlar chimney stacks. Planar surfaces rectified to true vertical alignment.
